validated_results.title: Calcium intake increases risk of prostate cancer among Singapore Chinese.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study investigating dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer risk in Singapore Chinese men.

sample_size.excerpt: We examined calcium intake and prostate cancer risk among 27,293 men of the Singapore Chinese Health Study that was established between 1993 and 1998. As of December 31, 2007, 298 incident prostate cancer cases had been diagnosed among the cohort members.
sample_size.location: Materials and Methods, Study Population, paragraph 1

cases.excerpt: As of December 31, 2007, 298 incident prostate cancer cases had been diagnosed among the cohort members.
cases.location: Materials and Methods, Study Population, paragraph 2

comparison.excerpt: Overall, we observed a modest, statistically nonsignificant 25% increase in prostate cancer risk for the 4 th (median = 659 mg/day) versus 1 st (median=211 mg/day) quartiles of calcium intake after adjustment for potential confounders.

design.excerpt: Utilizing the database of a prospective cohort of Singapore Chinese in whom dairy intake is low and calcium supplementation is rare, we will be able to assess the association between dietary calcium and prostate cancer

timing.excerpt: Person-years of follow-up were counted from the date of recruitment to the date of diagnosis of prostate cancer, death, migration, or December 31, 2007, whichever occurred first.
timing.location: Materials and Methods, Statistical Methods, paragraph 1
